title: Safe Harness Self-Evolution: A Theoretical Analysis of Feasibility and Limits
summary: Harness self-evolution is the process by which an agent modifies its prompts, tools, code, or orchestration in response to task feedback while keeping the underlying language model frozen, with changes persisting across subsequent tasks. We provide a systematic theoretical analysis of the feasibility and limits of safe harness self-evolution, connecting modification generation, finite-data certification and selection
body: Harness self-evolution is the process by which an agent modifies its prompts, tools, code, or orchestration in response to task feedback while keeping the underlying language model frozen, with changes persisting across subsequent tasks. We provide a systematic theoretical analysis of the feasibility and limits of safe harness self-evolution, connecting modification generation, finite-data certification and selection, safe adoption, and behavior after an update. Under a fixed user-task distribution, we establish conditions guaranteeing overall expected-reward improvement while controlling changes on retained tasks, characterize the probability of generating qualified modifications, and derive finite-data bounds for safe selection and adoption. Our analysis shows that generation and certification impose distinct constraints: current task performance does not determine the probability of generating qualified modifications, and generating more candidates need not improve the guarantee of a successful update when evaluation is limiting. Stagnation may therefore arise even when improvement opportunities remain. We further show that worst-case evaluation cost for recognizing genuine improvements diverges as expected reward approaches its upper bound. Across successive updates, certified improvement guarantees accumulate over a finite run, but a successful update does not by itself guarantee that further improvement remains possible. These results provide a basis for diagnosing bottlenecks and designing safer self-evolution mechanisms.
summaryZh: 该研究对智能体（agent）的“安全自我演化”（safe harness self-evolution）过程进行了系统的理论分析，该过程指智能体在保持底层语言模型冻结的前提下，根据任务反馈修改其提示、工具、代码或编排，并且这些修改会持续到后续任务。研究建立了修改生成、有限数据认证和选择、安全采纳以及更新后行为之间的联系。在固定用户-任务分布下，研究确立了保证整体期望回报提升并控制保留任务上变化的条件，刻画了生成合格修改的概率，并推导了安全选择和采纳的有限数据界限。分析表明，生成和认证施加了不同的约束，并且生成更多候选不一定能提高成功更新的保证。研究还指出，即使在改进机会存在的情况下也可能出现停滞，并且最坏情况下的评估成本会随着期望奖励接近上限而发散。
